classification.difficultyReason: Choose where to introduce a parallel construction, transfer the marked angles using corresponding or alternate angles, and combine or subtract them to prove the symbolic relationship; the prompt suggests construction but does not specify it.

content.prompt:
The questions may require construction lines to be drawn.

Example 8

spec.description: Broken line A–O–B with parallel horizontal rays AF and BG; the angle on the left at O is 120 degrees. Ordinary source blue is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: AF parallel BG; angle FAO is alpha; angle OBG is beta; angle AOB is 120 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; construction line omitted.

answer.short:
$\alpha+\beta=120^\circ$.

Draw a parallel through $O$ and use alternate angles.
answer.worked:
Construct $OP\parallel AF$, with $P$ to the left of $O$. Since $AF\parallel BG$, also $OP\parallel BG$.

$\angle AOP=\alpha$ and $\angle POB=\beta$ (alternate angles).

$$\begin{align*}\alpha+\beta&=\angle AOP+\angle POB\\\alpha+\beta&=\angle AOB\\\alpha+\beta&=120^\circ.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: V-shaped OF and OG; A and B lie on the respective arms. Upward AP and BQ are parallel. Ordinary source blue is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Angle FAP is 40 degrees; angle AOB is alpha; angle QBG is beta; AP parallel BQ.

answer.short:
$\alpha-\beta=40^\circ$.

Construct through $A$ a line parallel to $OG$ and use corresponding angles.
answer.worked:
Construct ray $AC\parallel OG$, pointing upwards and right.

$\angle FAC=\alpha$ (corresponding angles, $AC\parallel OG$).

$\angle PAC=\beta$ (corresponding angles, $AP\parallel BQ$ and $AC\parallel BG$).

$$\begin{align*}\alpha-\beta&=\angle FAC-\angle PAC\\\alpha-\beta&=\angle FAP\\\alpha-\beta&=40^\circ.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: AB rises to B; BE descends right. BC, FE and AD are parallel horizontal segments with matching arrowheads. Ordinary source blue is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Angle BAD is alpha; angle ABE is beta; angle BEF is 50 degrees; BC parallel FE parallel AD.

answer.short:
$\alpha+\beta=130^\circ$.

Alternate angles give $\angle CBE=50^\circ$; use co-interior angles on $AB$.
answer.worked:
$\angle CBE=50^\circ$ (alternate angles, $FE\parallel BC$).

$\angle ABC=\beta+50^\circ$ (adjacent angles).

$$\begin{align*}\alpha+\beta+50^\circ&=180^\circ\qquad(AD\parallel BC,\text{ co-interior angles})\\\alpha+\beta&=130^\circ.\end{align*}$$

teachingContext.methodNote: Use alternate and corresponding angles after constructing a parallel line, then combine adjacent angles or use supplementary co-interior angles.
teachingContext.mappingNote: Example 8 on pages 10–11 explicitly teaches introducing a parallel construction for symbolic angle proofs. Page 3 supplies the parallel-line properties used in all three parts.
